sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation, Initial TAVI Implantation and Early Complications
sections.description: This section outlines the patient’s baseline characteristics, the clinical context that led to the first transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), the early post‑implant course, and the complications that necessitated a second valve‑in‑valve (TAV‑in‑TAV) procedure.
subtopics: Late‑fifties to seventies male with multi‑vessel CAD, prior PCI, and comorbidities (HTN, DM, COPD, GI bleeding, pacemaker for AV block)
Initial severe aortic stenosis prompting 2014 Lotus TAVI (27 mm, self‑expanding, supra‑annular)
Early clinical trajectory: NYHA deterioration, progressive echocardiographic gradients, declining EF from 54% to 42%
Complication of TAV‑in‑TAV (Evolut 23 mm) in 2022: femoral hematoma and pseudoaneurysm managed surgically
Hemodynamic recovery after Evolut implantation: EF improvement to 54%

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Imaging Strategy for Repeat Intervention
sections.description: The diagnostic workup combined clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and advanced imaging to confirm structural valve deterioration, extrude active infection, and assess procedural feasibility for a third valve implantation.
subtopics: Indications for re‑intervention: mean gradient >35 mm Hg, severe regurgitation, symptomatic‑dyspnea, declining EF
Role of TTE and 3D TEE in quantifying stenosis, regurgitation, and detecting paravalvular leak
MSCT metrics: minimum lumen diameter (13.7 mm), sinuses dimensions, coronary ostial height, valve‑to‑coronary distance, neo‑skirt assessment
Infection resolution criteria: negative blood cultures, no vegetations on TEE, no paravalvular abscess
Surgical risk assessment: EuroSCORE II 27.36%, high STS risk, surgical infeasibility due to deep stent fixation and coronary proximity

sections.section_title: Procedural Planning and Technological Considerations for TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV
sections.description: This section details the pre‑procedural planning, valve selection, sizing strategies, and intra‑procedural techniques that enabled a safe and effective third valve deployment while minimizing risk of coronary obstruction and patient‑prosthesis mismatch.
subtopics: Valve choice: Acurate Neo2 self‑expanding, supra‑annular leaflets, low frame height suitable for narrow anatomies
Sizing methodology: annular measurement, predicted neo‑annulus, reference to 3‑D CT‑derived landmarks
High‑implant strategy: landing above the Evolut leaflets to preserve coronary clearance and limit PPM
Commissural alignment: use of CT‑guided markers and fluoroscopic angulation to maintain coronary access
Coronary protection assessment: CT‑derived coronary‑to‑prosthesis gap, decision to forego balloon‑guided protection
Pre‑ and post‑dilation protocol: 22/40 mm balloon pre‑dilation for valve expansion, 20/40 mm balloon post‑dilation under rapid pacing
Dual access (left radial, left femoral) under local anesthesia, rapid‑ventricular pacing for deployment
Intra‑procedural imaging: angiography for flow confirmation, aortography for valve position, TEE for leaflet motion

sections.section_title: Outcomes, Follow‑up and Clinical Evaluation of the Intervention
sections.description: This section reviews the immediate procedural success, early hemodynamic improvement, mid‑term functional status, and one‑year clinical and echocardiographic outcomes, applying Valve Academic Research Consortium‑3 criteria.
subtopics: Immediate VWR‑3 success: zero residual regurgitation, correct valve seating, no perivalvular leak, preserved coronary flow
Early Doppler data: mean gradient 67 mm Hg immediately, 27 mm Hg at 1 month, 26 mm Hg at 1 year; AVA 0.9→1.1 cm²; DVI 0.24
EF trajectory: 42% -> 54% after first TAV‑in‑TAV, 66% after third TAVI
Functional status: NYHA class improvement, exercise tolerance restoration, no re‑hospitalisation
Complication profile: absence of stroke, no paravalvular leak, no coronary obstruction, no recurrence of endocarditis
Long‑term surveillance plan: TTE at 3 months, 12 months, annular CT at 2 years, clinical visits every 6 months

sections.section_title: Clinical Implications, Guideline Context and Future Directions
sections.description: The final section contextualises the case within current guidelines, emphasises the rising need for lifelong planning of structural valve disease, and discusses potential future strategies for managing complex multi‑prosthesis anatomies.
subtopics: Guideline‑based management of prosthetic valve endocarditis: ESC 2025 recommendation vs. individualized strategy
Importance of early multidisciplinary planning to anticipate repeat TAVIs and preserve coronary access
Risk of patient‑prosthesis mismatch in serial TAV‑in‑TAVs and mitigation through high implantation
Emerging techniques: bioprosthetic valve fracture, BASILICA, leaflet laceration, and their applicability to triple‑stented anatomies
Limitations of surgical re‑explantation in high‑risk, heavily stented patients
Research gaps: dedicated imaging algorithms, computational flow dynamics, registry data on TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV outcomes
Future surveillance strategies: routine MSCT for neo‑annulus monitoring, integration of virtual‑flow simulation
